title: scope.policy/1
description: The configuration the sensor fetches. Immutable integer versions per customer; public to the customer; holds no secret (the sensor's validator refuses a secret-shaped value). A sensor that does not know a section ignores it; a rule kind it does not know runs as a skipped decision.

regex.description: a JavaScript regular expression over the path; anchored at the start by the compiler when it does not begin with ^; one that repeats a group holding a repeat, such as (a+)+, refuses the whole document

pattern.description: a regular expression over the page body with {host} filled in; applied globally

replacement.description: the replacement with $1 to $9 groups and {host}, {prefix}, {token} filled in; plain text, every link on https://{host} or a path, and on the html face only whole tags from a, blockquote, body, code, h1, head, html, li, meta, p, pre, title, ul with an a's href and a meta's utf-8 charset; on the md and txt faces no www or mail address, character reference, control character or markup a renderer would act on; anything else runs the rule dry. Where the pattern lands it inside a tag, an inline script or style, a title or a text area, or joins it to the page's text inside a word on the md or txt face, it only extends a link to https://{host} with a link-safe code. A rule that would grow a page past twice its size and 64 KiB is left out of it

fieldNames.description: the body field names a door's keys live in, by key kind; a sensor and the stitcher read the same names

bodyMatch.description: a body field and the value that means success

door.description: a door: its path pattern, or the pattern with the field names its keys live in

version.description: the customer's policy version; 0 is the embedded forward-only default

origin.description: ignored by the sensor: where traffic goes comes only from its own configuration (JOURNEYS_ORIGIN)

report.description: ignored by the sensor: records go to JOURNEYS_API_URL in its own configuration, with the install key as Authorization: Bearer

routes.description: the regular-expression form: four expressions over the path plus the text faces; a policy with surfaces ignores every key but run_prefix

run_prefix.description: a path prefix with two capture groups (the prefix, the rest): the path up to the rest group is stripped before classification and restored in rewritten links as {prefix}, whatever the first group captures

text_faces.description: plain-text documents that are pages (a root map such as llms.txt)

surfaces.description: the surface map: the roles of the product's paths, derived from the standards (MCP is one JSON-RPC endpoint carrying MCP-Session-Id and MCP-Protocol-Version; OAuth 2.1 names its registration (RFC 7591), authorization, token and device-authorization (RFC 8628) endpoints in its metadata documents (RFC 8414, RFC 9728); an API call carries a bearer) plus a short custom list. Classification precedence, first match wins: passthrough, custom (in order), finder, mcp, oauth.register, oauth.authorize, oauth.token, oauth.approve, device.start, device.poll, device.approve, hooks.create, hooks.catch, credentials, trial, cli.init, cli.beacon, signup, download, api, docs.llms and docs.root (docs_root), docs.paths (docs), else other.

paths.description: documentation pages: observed, content, references minted per serve

root.description: the site root or docs root page

llms.description: the root map (llms.txt), a plain-text page

faces.description: paths whose face is markdown or text regardless of the answer's content type

download.description: installer and package downloads: an opener of an install journey when the url carries a reference

actions.description: the API paths that are actions (a step with an outcome) rather than reads

action_success.description: what a successful action's answer says; absent means any 2xx

metadata.description: RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata; classified as api

resource_metadata.description: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata; classified as api

poll_approved.description: what the poll's answer says when the person approved; default {status: approved}

fields.description: device_code, user_code, approve_code (default code), credential (default api_key)

signup.description: the sign-up form post; fields: reference (default via)

catch.description: the first capture group is the hook id

trial.description: a trial key issued from code; fields: credential (default trial_key), install (default install_id)

init.description: the product's CLI registering a project or an install: an opener

beacon.description: the CLI's telemetry ping: an opener

cli.description: a regular expression over the user agent that names the customer's own CLI

sdk.description: the same for the customer's SDK

clients.description: how the reader family vendor-client is decided: the customer's own clients by pattern, never a hard-coded product string

finder.description: the documentation-finder route the sensor answers

custom.description: the customer's overrides, in order; an entry beats every standard entry

fields.description: body fields hashed by name wherever they appear, beside the names the sensor always hashes in bodies and URLs (api_key, key, token, access_token, refresh_token, id_token, code, client_secret, password, secret, signature, sig, in any case or spelling, or a name whose last word is key, token, secret, password, signature or sig; such a field's whole value is hashed unless it is true or false, except code in an answer's body (usually an error code); a valid reference code stays readable only where headers.reference or a door's fields.reference names the field)

shapes.description: the product's signed-value shapes, hashed wherever they appear: path, query, body, Location

uri_fields.description: a body field holding a url whose named parameter, in the query or the fragment, is a code; only that parameter's value is hashed

headers.description: the names of the headers the sensor reads; a name that is not a header name is ignored, and session, setup, agent, client and intent may not name one that carries a credential (a name with auth, cookie, token, secret, password, credential, key, jwt, assertion, oidc, signature, bypass, dpop, proof, hmac, csrf or xsrf in it, the credential header, surfaces.api.credential_header)

reference.description: the query parameters that carry a reference

headers.description: the policy's own x- headers added on the hop to the origin, with {host} filled in; x-forwarded, x-forwarded-*, x-real-ip, x-client-ip, x-cluster-client-ip, x-originating-ip, x-host, x-original-*, x-rewrite-url, x-http-method, x-http-method-override, x-method-override, x-middleware-*, x-invoke-*, x-matched-path, x-prerender-*, x-vercel-*, x-nextjs-*, x-journeys-*, x-scope-*, x-envoy-*, a name that carries a credential, a value that is not one line of latin-1 or has a placeholder other than {host}, and any name not starting x- are ignored

key_header.description: ignored by the sensor: the install key never goes to the origin; the signed assertion proves the hop

record_bodies.description: false is the lightest form: bodies are read where a rule needs them and never leave; true records, on the routes the surface map observes and for an error answer (400 or above) on any route it does not pass through, only the fields observe.bodies.allow_fields names, with secret names and shapes hashed; true with no allowed field records no body

observe.description: the body allowlist; routes, max_bytes and json_rpc are reserved and not read

allow_fields.description: the body field names that may leave, at any depth: an allowed field keeps its whole value, any other is dropped; a body with no allowed field is recorded as null

mode.description: dry_run computes what the rule would do, records it and changes nothing on the wire

environments.description: where a live rule is live; elsewhere it runs dry

on_error.description: closed is honoured by a gate only: the declaration call is refused instead of forwarded

faces.description: inject: a rewrite per face (html, md, txt); notfound: a page body per face, held to the same content as an inject replacement (with no html face, the md page is shown to a browser as escaped plain text)

route.description: finder and gate: the exact path; error: a regular expression over the path

default_links.description: finder: paths on the customer's site; anything else runs the rule dry

links.description: error: a path on the customer's site per status; anything else runs the rule dry

signers.description: the Web Bot Auth signers whose key directories the sensor fetches, each an exact https origin such as https://chatgpt.com (an entry that is not one is ignored and named in the notices); a signature from any other signer is recorded as unlisted_signer and causes no outbound request
